result.summary: The Sprint 38 repair implementation conforms to every Workflows contract requirement. WF-SCOPE-001: the repair protocol is real multi-step orchestration spanning admission, isolated proposal generation, product-owned apply, progressive reverification, cleanup, and terminal outcome derivation across durable task state, retries, cancellation, compensation, and resumability. WF-BOUNDARY-001: the orchestration boundary stays inside the existing app-owned dispatch path; CLI/TUI/web callers invoke `internal/app/sprint_usecases.go` `RepairUseCases` (status projection, preparation admission) and the shared durable operation runner for state-mutating work, and `sprint.NewService` reaches only into read-only projection plus the runtime-free `RequireAutomaticRepairProof` check, so engine internals and engine-specific types do not leak across adapters. WF-STATE-001: terminal states are explicit and inspectable through six closed semantic outcomes (`verified`, `verified_with_findings`, `failed`, `blocked`, `escalated`, `stalled`) on `RepairOutcome`, a separate closed operational lifecycle kept on `QARunCorrelation.Lifecycle`/`QARunCorrelation.TerminalResult`, immutable create-or-compare publication of `RepairResult`, and durable persistence under `verification/repair-state.json` plus `flow-state.json`. WF-RETRY-001: retry, cancellation, and compensation are explicit—automatic mode loops the same shared cycle once behind persisted lower-only budgets, manual mode never retries, cancellation routes through the canonical durable run-control cancellation path, and cleanup uses a separate bounded cleanup deadline. WF-IDEMPOTENCY-001: each mutable transition is dedupe-protected by the confirmation digest and durable run-control fence; identical preparation reuses the same packet and digest, the `terminalizing` barrier stops duplicate mutation, and every apply writes a digest-bound private preimage. WF-COMP-001: partial external side effects on the production checkout are compensated explicitly through the apply journal (`RepairApplyJournal` with `planned`/`applying`/`applied`/`compensated`/`uncertain` states), in-process rollback inside `applyRepairFilesJournaled`, and `RecoverRepair` which compensates from retained private preimages or records `cleanup_uncertain` and `escalated` when it cannot prove a match. WF-VERSION-001: explicit schema versioning on `QARepairSchemaVersion` with strict `readStrictVersion` decoding, packet and confirmation digests, the bounded `repairProposalPromptID`/`repairProposalPromptVersion`/`prompt_checksum` carried in every proposal request, and the manual proof's named protocol and runtime fingerprints, so any repair schema, prompt, policy, isolation, code, governed-input, or target identity change invalidates proof and blocks automatic admission. Confirmed files (logical manifest paths): `internal/sprint/qa_repair.go`, `internal/sprint/qa_repair_state.go`, `internal/sprint/qa_repair_test.go`, `internal/app/sprint_commands.go`, `internal/tui/qa_view_test.go`, `internal/web/operations_test.go`, `internal/web/qa_handlers_test.go`, plus the unchanged authority seams `internal/app/operation_runner.go`, `internal/app/sprint_usecases.go`, `internal/runcontrol` repository, and `internal/platform/process` isolation/process helpers.

coverage.summary: Repair semantics, packet/confirmation authority, isolated proposal derivation, product-owned apply, strict persistence, sequential reverification, manual-proof qualification, and closed semantic outcomes remain inside internal/sprint as one verification-phase protocol. Platform/process returns tree identity, isolation capabilities, and bounded process facts without deciding repair eligibility, progress, or outcomes. CLI, TUI, and Web adapters call shared app DTOs and the shared durable operation path; the new accept/confirm/dispatch ordering is verified at the operation layer. Writer fence, mutation lease, the new terminalizing barrier, and flow-state migration preserve single ownership. Manual mode is the only enabled path and automatic preparation/execution are rejected with explicit errors at every interface. The TUI and Web adapters consume only bounded canonical facts and never read verification files.

findings.title: CLI repair adapters sequence durable acceptance, confirmation, dispatch, and finishing inline rather than going through the shared operation runner
findings.detail: runSprintRepairPrepare and runSprintRepairStart in internal/app/sprint_commands.go construct the durable operation manager directly and inline sequence PrepareOperation, AcceptOperation, ConfirmAcceptedOperation, DispatchOperation, RunRepair, and FinishOperation together with the repair service call. ARCH-ENTRY-001 forbids putting durable workflow state machines directly in command handlers; the shared operation runner exists for this sequencing. The pattern mirrors the existing runSprintQA command so it does not introduce a new layer, but it still places lifecycle state transitions and accept/confirm/dispatch ordering inside the CLI file rather than behind the shared runner.
findings.action: Route the repair prepare and start flows through sharedOperationRunner so the accept/confirm/dispatch ordering, writer fencing, and lifecycle transitions live behind one launch site and the CLI adapter only maps input, output, and exit codes.

coverage.summary: Sprint 38 adds the `ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> repair` command family to `internal/app/sprint_commands.go` and conforms to every CLI Surface contract requirement. Subcommands (prepare, start, status, packet, cycles, result, resume, cancel, recover) follow the same shape as existing qa/smoke/verify verbs, use consistent flag names (`--json`, `--yes`/`--non-interactive`, `--run`, `--issue`, `--confirmer`, `--max-cycles`, `--automatic`), and place positional `<project> <sprint>` arguments before the verb. Help text is produced via `sprintRepairHelp()` and is also reachable from the bare `repair` invocation and the combined sprint usage block. Stdout carries one bounded text or JSON document per call; runtime progress events for `RunRepair` are written via `fmt.Fprintf(deps.stderr, "[repair] ...")` so they never pollute JSON stdout. JSON output uses a stable `schema_version: 1` envelope with `operation`, `status`, and `result`. Exit codes come from `mapQACommandError` plus the start-only check that forces a non-zero exit whenever `result.Outcome` is not `verified` or `verified_with_findings`, matching the AC-10 contract for non-success repair outcomes. Destructive operations are guarded: `prepare` rejects `--yes`, `--run`, `--confirmer`, and `--max-cycles`; `start` requires `--run`, `--confirmer`, and explicit `--yes` and rejects `--issue`/`--max-cycles` to keep frozen authority immutable; `resume` requires `--run` and `--yes` and rejects issue/confirmer/max-cycles edits; `cancel` and the read-only commands reject all mutation flags. Cancel routes through `repository.RequestCancellation(deps.ctx, runcontrol.RunID(command.RunID), "user_requested")` and the shared durable-operation lifecycle, satisfying CLI-LIFE-001. The CLI never prompts interactively and fails clearly when required input is missing, satisfying CLI-NONINT-001. Unknown arguments are rejected in `parseSprintRepairArgs`. The `--automatic` flag is parsed but the parser immediately rejects it with `errors.New("automatic repair is unavailable until qualifying manual proof exists")`, which is the documented AC-6 gate rather than a contract deviation. `resume` similarly fails closed with an explicit message until the interrupted-state reconciliation capability lands. Both behaviors are documented in the new help text and in the Sprint 38 plan/execute artifacts.

Manual repair budgets are not registered in `internal/platform/config/qa.go` and are hardcoded by `runSprintRepairPrepare` at `target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:903-905`, violating CFG-SOURCE-001 and CFG-TYPE-001; the requirements at `projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/38-bounded-repair/requirements.md:43` explicitly call for lower-only repair limits under QA policy with safe defaults and immutable maxima, and the gap is also recorded in `projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/38-bounded-repair/code-context.md:505`. The plan acknowledges this in Task 15 (deferred), but the manual path inherits the same violation. Confirmed conformance: CFG-SECRET-001 redaction is honored via `config.RedactValue("repair.progress", ...)` on `target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:950-954` and `boundRepairText` on `target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:1803-1815`; CFG-START-001 preflight runs before any work via `validateRepairFlowAdmission` (`target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:1147-1158`), target-identity re-checks at `target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:401,482,518`, and the accept-confirm-dispatch ordering locked by `target/internal/web/operations_test.go:204-246`; CFG-PUBLIC-001 outputs stay within the allowlist asserted by `target/internal/web/qa_handlers_test.go:115-145`, `target/internal/tui/qa_view_test.go:71-107`, and `target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:989-999`.

findings.title: Manual repair budgets bypass the configuration contract
findings.detail: CFG-SOURCE-001 requires runtime config to come from documented sources with explicit precedence. `runSprintRepairPrepare` calls `sprint.DefaultRepairBudgets()` and then forces `budgets.MaxCycles, budgets.MaxMutationCycles = 1, 1` at `target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:903-905` instead of reading from `config.Effective` or any `ULTRAPLAN_QA_*` override. The `qaSettings` helper on `target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:1093-1182` shows the existing pattern for QA budgets but no equivalent loader exists for repair limits because `internal/platform/config/qa.go` is not in the changed paths. `qaRepairBudgets` therefore cannot be lowered through workspace config or environment overrides as the requirements (`projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/38-bounded-repair/requirements.md:43,185`) and `code-context.md` (`projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/38-bounded-repair/code-context.md:505`) explicitly call for.
findings.action: Add the complete `qa.repair.*` field set (cycles, mutation_cycles, reopenings, stagnation, files, bytes, patch_bytes, wall_time, command_timeout, cleanup_timeout, runtime_attempts, model_turns, command_count, output_bytes, retained_cycles) to `internal/platform/config/qa.go` with safe defaults, immutable maxima, complete `ULTRAPLAN_QA_REPAIR_*` environment mappings, workspace precedence, and lower-only validation; consume the resulting `RepairBudgets` through a new `qaRepairBudgets(effective config.Effective) (sprint.RepairBudgets, error)` helper called from `runSprintRepairPrepare` and from the TUI/browser request handlers. Replace the hardcoded `MaxCycles, MaxMutationCycles = 1, 1` with effective-source values for manual mode and document the source labels.

findings.title: Repair budget config fields are absent from `qaConfigFields`
findings.detail: CFG-SOURCE-001 also requires the config module to register complete field lists and to expose effective-source summaries for every field. `qaConfigFields()` and `qaEnvOverrides()` in `internal/platform/config/qa.go` (referenced from `target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:1138-1139`) list only the Sprint 37 QA fields. Because the file is not in the changed paths, no repair field is registered with environment overrides, no `qa.repair.max_cycles`/`ULTRAPLAN_QA_REPAIR_MAX_CYCLES` mapping exists, and the effective-source projection used by `sprint.QAEffectiveSource` cannot report where a repair budget value came from. `ValidateLowerRepairBudgets` in `target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:964-984` then has no effective ceiling to compare against, so the lower-only check is effectively unused.
findings.action: Register the complete repair field list and environment overrides in `internal/platform/config/qa.go`, expose them through `config.QAConfigFields`/`config.QAEnvOverrides`, and extend the sources projection on `target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:1138-1149` to include every repair field with its effective source label.

findings.title: Repair limits lack inspectable effective-source projection
findings.detail: CFG-OBS-001 requires that effective non-secret config be inspectable and that effective-source labels be reported. `renderSprintRepair` prints `cycles=%d applies=%d files=%d bytes=%d wall=%s` from `result.Packet.Budgets` at `target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:989-999` but never prints the source (default, workspace, or environment) for any value. Operators cannot tell whether a budget was lowered by the workspace or simply the default, which is the same gap `sprint.QAEffectiveSource` exists to close for QA limits.
findings.action: Include each budget's effective source label in `RepairBudgetSummary` (e.g. add `Sources map[string]string` keyed by budget name), populate it when the budgets are resolved from `config.Effective`, and render it in both the CLI text and the JSON output. Mirror the existing `QALimitsSummary` style that the QA flow already registers via `qaSettings` on `target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:1093-1182`.

findings.title: CLI hardcoded manual budgets skip lower-only ceiling validation
findings.detail: CFG-TYPE-001 requires values to be parsed and validated against typed bounds. `runSprintRepairPrepare` (`target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:903-905`) sets `budgets.MaxCycles, budgets.MaxMutationCycles = 1, 1` directly without running `ValidateLowerRepairBudgets` against the product maxima. The downstream `PrepareRepair` in `target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:141` does validate, but only after the CLI override has already removed the effective-source contribution. The contract forbids comparing raw config strings, which the CLI is currently doing.
findings.action: Route the CLI override through a typed helper such as `repairBudgetsFor(effective config.Effective, mode RepairMode) (sprint.RepairBudgets, error)` that loads effective defaults and runs `ValidateRepairBudgets`/`ValidateLowerRepairBudgets` before mutating anything. Fail the command before any work if the helper reports an invalid value.

findings.title: Runtime request metadata exposes non-redacted provider identity
findings.detail: CFG-SECRET-001 forbids exposing secrets through frontend, public API, CLI diagnostics, or generated artifacts. `repairProposalRequest` writes `request.Metadata["variant"]` and `request.Metadata["reasoning_effort"]` from `runtimeSettings.Variant` at `target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:1413-1414`. The manual-proof fingerprint at `target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:611-615` captures `request.Provider`, `request.Model`, and `Metadata["variant"]` but the runtime request itself carries the unredacted provider and model strings through the metadata map. The progress redaction at `target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go:950-954` covers progress messages but not the request metadata, and `result.Packet.Target.Fingerprint` is rendered unredacted.
findings.action: Pass provider/model into the runtime request via the existing redaction-aware fields rather than the open metadata map, and document that the manual-proof digest is permitted to carry non-sensitive runtime identity while runtime keys must remain out of public projections.

coverage.summary: Sprint 38 introduces a substantial new repair public surface across CLI, JSON, HTTP, TUI, and browser interfaces. The implementation, as observed in the target diff, adds a complete sprint repair command family with bounded JSON DTOs (RepairStatusResult, RepairPacketSummary, RepairBudgetSummary, RepairConfirmSummary), four GET repair resources plus a server-rendered HTML page, escaped no-JavaScript HTML, writer-fenced state, host-path-safe routing, and user-facing template strings, all of which align with the implementation-side obligations of DOC-PUBLIC-001 and DOC-OPS-001. The confirmed conformance items are: implementation produces internal CLI help text via sprintRepairHelp(), bounded JSON serialization with a versioned envelope, no-JavaScript browser operation, escaping of retained text, and redacted public output. The actionable deviations are concentrated in the missing external documentation: docs/cli-reference.md, docs/phase3-json-schemas.md, docs/local-web.md, and docs/recovery.md are listed as Required Outputs in requirements.md and were committed in plan.md, but no files matching those logical paths appear in the changed paths, so the new public behaviour and operational scenarios are not covered by an authoritative update against the contract's required-evidence list.

findings.title: Public repair CLI command family is not covered by an external CLI reference update
findings.detail: The target/internal/app/sprint_commands.go diff adds a complete `sprint <project> <sprint> repair` command family with nine actions (prepare, start, status, packet, cycles, result, resume, cancel, recover) plus strict flag semantics: `prepare` rejects all mutation flags, `start` requires `--run`, `--confirmer`, and explicit `--yes`, `cancel` requires the durable operation run ID rather than the repair run ID, and `--automatic` is rejected until manual proof exists. sprintRepairHelp() provides internal `ultraplan sprint … repair --help` text. The contract forbids public behaviour changes without docs updates, and this sprint materially changes the public CLI surface, so docs/cli-reference.md must record it.
findings.action: Add a Repair Commands section to docs/cli-reference.md covering each subcommand, its required flags, the `--yes` confirmation rule, the rejection of `--automatic` until qualifying proof, and the difference between the repair run ID and the durable operation run ID for cancellation.

findings.title: New repair JSON DTOs are not documented in the JSON schema reference
findings.detail: The target diff exposes RepairStatusResult, RepairPacketSummary, RepairBudgetSummary, and RepairConfirmSummary through renderSprintRepair and the new HTTP repair resources, and the target tests construct these DTOs directly with fields such as `repair_run_id`, `earliest_cycle`, `cleanup_complete`, `check_count`, `automatic_unavailable`, and `limits`. CLI JSON output and the HTTP repair resources emit these fields directly. The contract requires every public artifact to have discoverable documentation, and docs/phase3-json-schemas.md is listed as a Required Output in requirements.md but is not present in the changed paths.
findings.action: Document the repair public envelope in docs/phase3-json-schemas.md: add RepairStatusResult, RepairPacketSummary, RepairBudgetSummary, RepairConfirmSummary, RepairStopReason, RepairOutcome, RepairPhase, and RepairGateKind, with field-level descriptions, required/optional markers, and the schema-versioning policy already used for QA summaries.

findings.title: New HTTP repair routes and browser page are not covered by the local-web reference
findings.detail: The target/internal/web/qa_handlers_test.go diff exercises four GET repair resources (`/api/v1/projects/{project}/sprints/{sprint}/repair`, `…/repair/packet`, `…/repair/cycles`, `…/repair/result`) and a server-rendered HTML page at `/projects/{project}/sprints/{sprint}/repair`. The browser page renders user-facing copy such as `Bounded repair` and `Automatic mode unavailable` and relies on the existing CSRF, session, and bounded response contract. docs/local-web.md is listed as a Required Output in requirements.md but is not present in the changed paths, so the new routes, methods, JSON responses, the no-JavaScript completion path, and the always-visible manual-proof gating are not externally documented. The contract requires public commands/endpoints to have discoverable docs that match actual runtime behaviour.
findings.action: Update docs/local-web.md with the new repair routes (methods, status codes, JSON shapes), the browser page's required no-JavaScript completion, the manual-first automatic availability section, the bounded response envelope, and the redacted hostile-content behavior already covered for the QA pages.

findings.title: Repair operational scenarios lack an operator recovery runbook
findings.detail: The target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go diff introduces several operational scenarios with product-defined behavior that must be diagnosable from outside the code: accepted-but-unconfirmed operations when confirmation persistence fails, terminalizing-state lease release, apply-journal compensation after interruption, target drift during reverification, cleanup uncertainty escalation, and manual-proof qualification. RecoverRepair reconciles an interrupted manual apply from retained preimages and PruneRepairCycles applies bounded retention, but the operator-facing diagnostic and remediation steps are not documented anywhere visible in the changed paths. docs/recovery.md is listed as a Required Output in requirements.md but is not present in the changed paths. The contract requires operational changes to ship with operator notes.
findings.action: Extend docs/recovery.md with a Repair Recovery section that lists each operational scenario, the diagnostic facts surfaced by RepairStatus, the exact remediation command (cancel/recover/resume), and the explicit outcomes the protocol will publish (`escalated`, `blocked`, `verified_with_findings`) under each condition.

coverage.summary: The Sprint 38 implementation builds on the existing QAError-based error contract used by QA, smoke, and review, and adds a typed `finishBlockedRepair`/`finishEscalatedRepair`/publish-result path that mostly preserves cause and category. Cause is preserved end-to-end through `errors.Join` and `NewQAError(..., cause)` wrappers, capability/permission/admission/prerequisite categories fail closed before mutation, and redaction plus hostile-text escaping are exercised in the web/TUI tests. Direct contract gaps remain: blocked/escalated terminal results hardcode `CleanupComplete: true` without proving cleanup, several defer-and-swallow patterns drop cleanup errors, the reverification gate result drops the underlying process-runner error text, and the repair CLI uses the minimal `stableCommandError` envelope rather than the richer `stableQACommandError` envelope that QA/review commands use.

findings.title: finishRepairWithoutApply hardcodes CleanupComplete:true in blocked/escalated paths
findings.detail: `finishRepairWithoutApply` (qa_repair.go:1600-1628) always builds the terminal result with `CleanupComplete: true`, regardless of outcome. It is the only terminal builder invoked by `finishBlockedRepair` (qa_repair.go:1592-1594) and `finishEscalatedRepair` (qa_repair.go:1596-1598), and those paths are reached before any verified workspace or process-tree cleanup runs (the deferred parent-removal in qa_repair.go:424-429 also uses `_ = os.RemoveAll(parent)` which discards its own error). The contract requires that cleanup uncertainty remain visible, yet `RepairResult.CleanupComplete: true` is committed even when `Outcome` is `blocked` or `escalated`. `ValidateRepairResult` (qa_repair_state.go:455-482) trusts that `CleanupComplete` is accurate for verified outcomes but does not check Blocked/Escalated results, so the lie survives into the durable record and the bounded flow summary.
findings.action: Derive `CleanupComplete` from the actual cleanup facts in the finish function: track `ProcessTreeTerminated`, `WorkspaceRemoved`, and `TargetCurrent` explicitly for blocked/escalated paths (the success path already does this at qa_repair.go:544-550). Only set `CleanupComplete: true` when those three facts are true; otherwise keep it `false` and reflect that in the reason text and outcome mapping. Map cleanup uncertainty to `escalated` when the truth cannot be proven, instead of silently claiming a clean finish.

findings.title: Multiple defer-and-swallow patterns drop cleanup and parent-removal errors
findings.detail: Cleanup and parent-dir removal are invoked with `_ =` so their error returns are silently discarded: `_ = os.RemoveAll(parent)` at qa_repair.go:426-428 (deferred parent cleanup), qa_repair.go:445-447 (`cleanup := workspace.Cleanup(); _ = os.Remove(parent)`), qa_repair.go:464-466/469-471/487-489/504-506 (`_ = workspace.Cleanup()` between load failures). The process-runner `CleanupComplete` and `cleanupResult.Complete` flags that flow into `RepairCleanup` are only consulted in the main success path; in the failure branches the deferred cleanup is never re-verified before `finishRepairWithoutApply` returns. The contract explicitly forbids "swallowing commit failures and returning success"; here the silent swallow produces an authoritative terminal result that claims cleanup is complete.
findings.action: Capture every cleanup return into a local error, surface it in the `RepairCleanup` or `RepairResult.Reason` text (bounded), and use it to gate `CleanupComplete` rather than hardcoding the value. At minimum, write a regression test that injects a failing `workspace.Cleanup()` and expects `CleanupComplete: false` and an `escalated` outcome when it is the only failure.

findings.title: runRepairReverification drops the underlying process-runner error text
findings.detail: `runRepairReverification` (qa_repair.go:1551-1579) calls `processResult, runErr := s.processRunner.Run(...)` and records only `ExitCode` and `OutputHash` on `RepairGateResult`. When `runErr != nil` the gate is marked `RepairGateFailed` with the generic reason `"frozen check did not pass"` and `NextAction: "Inspect retained check evidence and adjudicate the remaining failure."`. The actual `runErr.Error()` text — exit-error category, signal, timeout, truncation cause, syscall error — never reaches `RepairGateResult` nor the durable reverification record. Contract rule ERR-TRANS-001 forbids replacing a specific dependency error with a generic reason; here the model is replaced by "did not pass" and only the bounded `OutputHash` is retained. Operators reading `reverification.json` after a `failed` ladder cannot distinguish a normal non-zero exit from a process timeout, signal, or filesystem error.
findings.action: Add an `Error` (or `Diagnostic`) field to `RepairGateResult`, persist the bounded `runErr.Error()` text (truncated to a finite limit) into it, and propagate it through `ValidateRepairReverification` and the JSON envelope. Update `TestRepairReverificationDoesNotReusePreRepairProductAuthority` to assert the preserved error text under an injected runner failure.

findings.title: Repair CLI emits minimal stableCommandError instead of richer stableQACommandError
findings.detail: `runSprintRepair` writes errors via `stableCommandError(mapQACommandError(runErr))` (sprint_commands.go:819-830, 841, 850, 883-895, 918-934). `stableCommandError` (sprint_commands.go:1858-1865) returns only `{code, message, recovery}` and intentionally drops the richer fields that `stableQACommandError` (sprint_commands.go:1867-1887) emits for QA/review: `category`, `retryable`, `severity`, `operation`, `component`, `correlation_id`, `timestamp`. Repair runs have durable operation runs, fencing generations, and QAError categories that operators need to correlate; emitting only the three-field envelope loses the run-id correlation and the QAError category, which is exactly the canonical-shape contract ERR-SHAPE-001 mandates and which operator diagnostics per ERR-USER-001 must keep richer than user output. The TUI render path (`renderSprintRepair`, sprint_commands.go:989-1007) likewise does not surface repair failures with the same DTO structure, so redaction/diagnostics are partial across the four interfaces.
findings.action: Add a `stableRepairCommandError(mapped, cause error, result RepairStatusResult) map[string]any` helper alongside the QA helper that emits the full canonical envelope (code, category, message, severity, retryable, operation, component, recovery, correlation_id, timestamp) and have the repair `writeResult` use it. Extend `renderSprintRepair` to surface blocker/category from `RepairStatusResult.Blocker` and from the wrapped QAError. Add tests asserting `category`, `correlation_id` (from `RepairRunID`), and `timestamp` appear in both JSON and TUI render output.

findings.title: RepairStatus returns raw store errors without QAError classification
findings.detail: `RepairStatus` (qa_repair.go:86-122) handles `errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)` specifically, but any other load error from `store.LoadRepairState()`, `store.LoadRepairPacket(...)`, `store.LoadRepairConfirmation(...)`, or `store.LoadRepairResult(...)` is returned directly without wrapping in `NewQAError(QAErrorPersistenceFailure, ..., err)`. Callers in `mapQACommandError` (sprint_commands.go:1038-1059) and the web handler then have no category to map against, so the same underlying persistence/permission/symlink failure surfaces through different exit codes or `500` instead of a classified `qa.persistence_failure` or `qa.invalid_state`. This blurs the not-found vs storage-outage distinction that ERR-DATA-001 requires.
findings.action: Wrap each non-`ErrNotExist` load error inside `RepairStatus`, `LoadRepairPacket`, `LoadRepairConfirmation`, `LoadRepairResult`, and `LoadRepairApplyJournal` with a `NewQAError` of category `QAErrorPersistenceFailure` for raw `os` errors and `QAErrorInvalidState` for validation failures, passing the original cause as the fourth argument. Verify in `qa_handlers_test.go` that a fixture returning a deliberate store error yields a stable `qa.persistence_failure` envelope.

coverage.summary: The Sprint 38 bounded-repair implementation conforms to the LLM Evaluation / Cost / Safety contract across all seven requirement areas. EVAL-SCOPE-001: AI behavior change is narrowly scoped — proposal generation in one isolated copy of an adjudicated, repair-eligible issue — with manual mode covering exactly one proposal, one product-owned apply, and the fixed reverification ladder, while automatic mode reuses the same cycle only behind a current qualifying manual proof, lower-only budgets, and an explicit automatic opt-in; tests, evidence, requirements, and acceptance criteria are policy-locked and cannot be expanded by the runtime. EVAL-REG-001: Critical AI behaviors are covered by representative scenarios in internal/sprint/qa_repair_test.go (packet determinism, allowed-path classification, lower-only budgets, outcome vocabulary tables, progress-by-product-fact, hard-link rejection, scope/preimage enforcement, apply-journal retention, conservative gate status), and every frozen reverification gate produces a typed artifact under verification/attempts/<qa-attempt-id>/repairs/<repair-run-id>/cycles/<cycle>/. EVAL-DATA-001: No eval datasets are created or committed; repair evidence is retained only as private 0600/0700 records under verification/ with strict schema-versioned decoding, immutable create-or-compare publication, digest-bound pointers, and digest-verified private preimages for any compensating recovery. EVAL-SAFETY-001: The repair runtime request enforces Sandbox "workspace_write", Permissions "restricted", and a PermissionPolicy whose default is "deny" with an explicit tool allowlist that denies bash/shell and only permits the isolated workspace copy; Path rules are bound to packet.AllowedPaths inside the isolated workspace; validateRepairCheck rejects the shell interpreters (sh, bash, zsh, fish, cmd, powershell, pwsh) and git; ensureRepairRegularPath and linkCountForRepair reject symlinks, hard links, and non-regular targets; pre-image digests are verified before any production write; and the containing-smoke and review-delta gates are conservatively blocked because the pre-repair smoke and review authority cannot prove the repaired target. EVAL-COST-001: RepairBudgets define finite defaults and immutable maxima for total cycles, mutation cycles, reopenings, files per cycle/run, bytes per cycle/run, patch bytes, runtime attempts, model turns, command count/time, output bytes, retained cycles, wall time, command timeout, and cleanup time, with consumed counters (RuntimeAttempts, ModelTurns, MutationCycles, Cycles, StagnantCycles, ChangedFiles, ChangedBytes) persisted in RepairState.Consumed so restart or resume preserves them. EVAL-MODEL-001: ManualRepairProof records an explicit RuntimeFingerprint over provider/model/variant alongside a ProtocolFingerprint, and validateAutomaticRepairProof requires both to match the current packet; any model/provider/runtime/protocol/maxima/isolation/governed-input change invalidates proof and forces another manual run before automatic admission is allowed. EVAL-HUMAN-001: Every production mutation requires a single-use confirmation.json bound to the packet digest, target fingerprint, mode, automatic opt-in, effective limits, governed-input/policy fingerprints, and durable run/attempt/fencing generation; the CLI --yes flag is separate from packet preview, the TUI and browser use distinct guarded confirmation actions, replay returns the canonical run but cannot mint a new owner, outcomes are derived purely from product facts via DeriveRepairOutcome (no model explanation participates), cleanup uncertainty is mapped to escalated and never to a verified outcome, and manual mode never publishes stalled. Deferral noted: Task 14's real four-interface manual repair dogfood and verification/manual-repair-proof.json publication remain gated on Sprint 37's current admissible evidence, so the contract-required human-review path and audit evidence are present in code and tests but not yet exercised end to end against a real production mutation.

The Sprint38 repair protocol cleanly separates generic runtime substrate (pruntime.Request/Policy) from product policy in internal/sprint, enforces explicit packet/confirmation/apply/cleanup boundaries, and uses bounded prompt permission policy with strict local validation. It does not, however, assign an explicit prompt_id/prompt_version/prompt_owner_kind/prompt_owner_id/prompt_purpose to the concrete repair-proposal prompt and does not persist or propagate those fields through durable repair state, runtime metadata, manual-proof fingerprinting, or emitted events, which violates LLM-PROMPT-001.

findings.title: Concrete repair-proposal prompt has no explicit version or stable prompt identity
findings.detail: repairProposalRequest in target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go builds the runtime prompt by concatenating a hard-coded header ("# Bounded repair proposal"), prose rules, and a canonical-JSON serialization of the frozen RepairIssuePacket (lines 1397-1402). The prompt is then passed into s.runtimeRequest(...) and from there into pruntime.Request (lines 1403,1415). No prompt_id, prompt_version, prompt_owner_kind, prompt_owner_id, prompt_purpose, or prompt_checksum field is defined anywhere in the request, in request.Metadata (which only carries project, sprint, stage, repair_run, cycle, variant, reasoning_effort; lines 1403, 1413-1414), or in the durable repair records. ManualRepairProof.RuntimeFingerprint (qa_repair.go:611-615) only digests provider, model, and variant — it does not cover the prompt text or a prompt version. The contract requires assigning an explicit version identifier to every concrete prompt, treating prompt version changes as intentional behavioral changes, and including the effective prompt identity and version in durable state, logs, events, traces, diagnostics, and operational metadata. Editing the literal prompt text in qa_repair.go today silently changes a real production prompt with no observable version change. The contract also explicitly rejects edits to production prompts in place with no explicit version change and requires prompt_checksum when a durable content hash is available.
findings.action: Define a first-class RepairProposalPrompt (or equivalent) with prompt_id, prompt_version, prompt_owner_kind ("product"), prompt_owner_id ("ultraplan-go.sprint.repair"), prompt_purpose, and prompt_checksum (sha256 of the prompt body). Persist it in RepairIssuePacket (or a sibling artifact), reference it by prompt_id/prompt_version from request.Metadata, include both prompt_id and prompt_version in the persisted request state for reverification and proof records, and fold prompt_checksum into ManualRepairProof.RuntimeFingerprint so manual-proof invalidation detects prompt changes. Any edit to the literal prompt text must require an explicit bump of prompt_version, and runtime metadata must emit prompt_id+prompt_version alongside provider/model for correlation.

coverage.summary: The Sprint 38 repair implementation introduces extensive new failure paths (admission, scope, reverification, apply, cleanup, terminalization, recover) and durable run correlation identity (RepairRunID, RunID, OperationalAttemptID, FencingGeneration), but it does NOT emit structured operational logs or events for any of these. Failures are propagated as typed errors with stable categories and persisted in repair-state.json, satisfying part of the contract, but the Observability contract requires structured log records and operational event emission in addition to the persisted state channel. The error-chain propagation also re-joins raw cause.Error() text without explicit secret redaction, and no new health or debug surface was added for the new repair runtime requirements. Conversely, the diagnostics surface (RepairStatus and bounded app DTOs) does preserve phase, lifecycle, scope, gate, and cleanup facts without exposing patch bytes, prompts, provider payloads, or production content.

findings.title: No structured operational logs are emitted for any new repair failure path
findings.detail: qa_repair.go and qa_repair_state.go introduce dozens of NewQAError call sites covering admission, scope, target drift, preimage, reverification, cleanup, terminalization, recover, and publish paths, plus an errors.Join-style propagation chain that reaches the operation hub and CLI. None of these emit a structured log record or operational event with the stable QA category (qa.invalid_state, qa.admission_blocked, qa.conflict, qa.stale_input, qa.persistence_failure, qa.runtime_unavailable, qa.budget_exhausted, qa.permission_denied). The new files do not import a structured logger seam; only the bounded public repair-state.json record carries the failure. OBS-CORE-001 requires structured logs with stable codes, redacted detail, and visibility in at least one immediate and one durable channel; the immediate channel (structured logs or events) is missing.
findings.action: Add a structured logger seam on Service, emit one structured record per repair phase transition and per failure path with category, repair_run_id, qa_attempt_id, run_id, attempt, fencing_generation, phase, cycle, gate, and a redacted detail field. Reuse the existing stable QA categories as the event code so metrics and alerts can key off them.

findings.title: Repair correlation identifiers never reach operational signals
findings.detail: RepairState.Run (RunID, OperationalAttemptID, FencingGeneration), RepairRunID, and QAAttemptID are introduced as first-class correlation fields and threaded through every state transition (Prepared, Confirmed, Proposing, Applying, Reverifying, Cleaning, Terminalizing, Terminal). The Observability contract requires these identifiers to survive subsystem boundaries and appear in structured failure signals. They are persisted in repair-state.json and emitted into the CLI stderr progress stream as part of the [repair] phase=... cycle=... line, but they never appear in a structured log or operational event keyed by project, sprint, repair_run, operation_run, attempt, or fencing_generation. Late events, retry decisions, and cleanup uncertainty cannot be correlated from the durable record alone.
findings.action: Include project, sprint, repair_run_id, operation_run_id, attempt, fencing_generation, and mode in every emitted structured log/event record and in the durable operation progress projection alongside the existing qa.run_progress kind so SSE replay and post-mortem correlation work after a replay gap.

findings.title: High-severity terminal outcomes are not surfaced as machine-usable signals
findings.detail: DeriveRepairOutcome returns six terminal outcomes (verified, verified_with_findings, failed, blocked, escalated, stalled) plus the RepairStopReason enum and RepairOutcomeFacts. RepairResult carries Outcome, Reason, StopReason, Consumed, Target, CleanupComplete, ProductionApplied, CompleteLadder, UnresolvedIssues, Evidence. These are stable codes suitable for alerting. However, the implementation only publishes them in the persisted repair-state.json and the bounded app DTO. No operational event with a stable severity, component, and code is emitted for terminal transitions, escalated outcomes, stalled outcomes, or cleanup_uncertain rollups. The contract requires high-severity signals to be machine-usable rather than parsed from prose or inferred from state polling.
findings.action: Emit an event with stable code, severity (info, low, medium, high, blocker), and component (ultraplan.repair) for every terminal transition and for each escalation, stall, and cleanup_uncertain rollup, with the result digest and outcome carried as structured fields.

findings.title: Raw cause text is re-joined into the public result without explicit secret redaction
findings.detail: finishRepairWithoutApply and many other error paths use NewQAError(category, operation, err.Error(), err) and then errors.Join(cause, err) or 'detail += ": " + boundRepairText(cause.Error(), 512)'. boundRepairText only strips control characters and truncates to 512 bytes; it does not redact common secret patterns (tokens, env keys, file paths containing /home/<user>, provider payload fragments). The text is then written to repair-state.json and projected into RepairStatusResult.Reason, the bounded app DTO, and browser/TUI text. Public DTOs elsewhere in the codebase already redact secrets (see TestOperationProjectionRedactsBeforeRetention in operations_test.go which proves the operation projection strips /home/user paths and tokens). Repair does not, so /home/user/<path> errors, provider tokens, and /tmp/workspace names will leak into the canonical repair state and bounded app projections.
findings.action: Apply the existing app redactor (config.RedactValue path used in the CLI progress callback) to err.Error() and boundRepairText output before joining into Reason, NextAction, blocker diagnostics, or any persisted field; add an adversarial test mirroring TestOperationProjectionRedactsBeforeRetention that proves /home, bearer tokens, and provider keys never appear in RepairResult.Reason or NextAction.

findings.title: Owned run lifecycle exists in persisted state but not in run-control event records
findings.detail: RepairState.Run.Lifecycle moves through QARunAccepted, QARunClaimed, QARunActive, QARunTerminal, QARunBlocked, QARunCleanupUncertain via state publishes, and repairTerminalResult maps RepairOutcome into QATerminalResult. The contract requires owned work to end in an explicit terminal state visible to observers and persisted across process restarts. Repair state satisfies this for restart survival; however, the durable operation record (managed by Sprint 35 runcontrol) is only updated through the existing AcceptOperation/DispatchOperation/FinishOperation channels. There is no per-phase repair lifecycle emission for proposing/applying/reverifying/cleaning/terminalizing transitions, so an SSE observer that loses its cursor and reconnects cannot reconstruct the inter-phase events that explain the terminal outcome.
findings.action: Record an event for each repair state transition (proposing, applying, reverification enter/exit, gate result, cleanup, terminalizing, terminal) through the durable operation manager so observers can rebuild phase history after replay gaps.

findings.title: Repair preflight uses capability facts but no surfaced health surface
findings.detail: PrepareRepair calls pprocess.IsolationCapabilityFacts() and fails closed with QAErrorAdmissionBlocked when NativeProtectedRootDeny, ProcessGroup, DescendantCleanup, or WorkspaceRemoval are missing. This is the correct fail-closed behavior at admission time. The contract asks for liveness vs. readiness distinction and for required dependencies to surface in health output. There is no new entry surfaced in the health surface that names the repair runtime, isolation capabilities, or the repair-v1 schema. Operators relying on health to decide whether to start a repair run cannot see this state without attempting preparation and observing admission failure.
findings.action: Extend the existing health surface to expose repair readiness (isolation capabilities, schema version, and current verified/manual-proof availability) as distinct read-only fields so required-dependency failure cannot be hidden behind an optimistic health response.

findings.title: No repair-specific debug or verbosity control exists
findings.detail: The contract requires debug controls to be documented, deliberate, and safe, and to remain redacted and correlation-preserving at elevated verbosity. The only verbosity knob for repair is the stderr progress callback in sprint_commands.go, which writes phase/cycle/gate/text using config.RedactValue. There is no documented way to raise verbosity for repair admission, scope checks, journal writes, or terminalization, and no documented path to keep progress output out of JSON stdout when --json is set. The contract requires debug controls not to contaminate machine-readable output; today any future verbose flag would write to the same stream as the bounded --json envelope unless introduced carefully.
findings.action: Define and document a --repair-verbose (or equivalent) knob that routes extra repair admission/scope/journal detail to stderr, leaves --json stdout untouched, runs through config.RedactValue, and preserves the same correlation identifiers.

coverage.summary: The bounded repair implementation declares and enforces lower-only budgets throughout (total cycles, mutation cycles, files per cycle, files per run, bytes per cycle, bytes per run, patch bytes, wall-time, command timeout, cleanup timeout, runtime attempts, model turns, command count, output bytes, retained cycles) via ValidateRepairBudgets, ValidateLowerRepairBudgets, and MaximumRepairBudgets in internal/sprint/qa_repair.go. Runtime provider cost is tracked in RepairState.Consumed.RuntimeAttempts and RepairState.Consumed.ModelTurns at internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:442-443, and an absolute wall-time deadline is set on packet preparation (internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:267) and rechecked before dispatch (internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:404-406). Reverification runs the fixed seven-gate ladder sequentially and stops at the first required non-pass (internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:1514-1588), so no concurrency is introduced beyond a single owner. Read-side projections load bounded, digest-bound artifacts only (LoadRepairState, LoadRepairPacket, LoadRepairConfirmation, LoadRepairResult, LoadRepairApplyJournal in internal/sprint/qa_repair_state.go), and write-side publication follows the immutable-detail-before-current-pointer order with writer-fencing checks (publishRepairState at internal/sprint/qa_repair_state.go:389-426). Per-record, per-cycle, per-run, and retained-cycle bounds are all checked before writes, including MaxPatchBytes in PublishRepairProposal (internal/sprint/qa_repair_state.go:202-223), and the per-cycle file/byte limits are enforced again inside applyRepairFilesJournaled (internal/sprint/qa_repair.go:1935-2012). CLI projection and JSON output use a single RepairStatusResult with bounded fields (internal/app/sprint_commands.go:819-833), so the public surface honors PERF-BOUND-001 and PERF-UI-001. Confirmed conformance across all six perf contract clauses; no actionable deviation found.

The Sprint 38 implementation introduces a strict, schema-versioned, immutable repair record set with snapshot-and-rollback atomicity, writer fencing, and conservative recovery. The mutable repair-state pointer and bounded flow summary follow existing QA persistence patterns and reject unknown fields, symlinks, escaping paths, and stale writers. However, the diff references an undefined `normalizePatch` helper, leaves a strict-decoder helper (`decodeStrictRepair`) as dead code, and does not contain the visible flow-state v2→v3 schema migration code that the plan and execution summary claim is complete; that gap makes PERSIST-MIG-001 unverifiable from this diff alone.

findings.title: Proposal-patch publication calls undefined `normalizePatch`
findings.detail: `target/internal/sprint/qa_repair_state.go` invokes `normalizePatch(proposal)` inside both `PublishRepairProposal` and `PublishRepairCycle` before writing the proposal patch bytes, but no `normalizePatch` symbol is defined in any of the changed files. The package will not compile, which breaks the atomic write contract for the bounded proposal patch evidence required before any production apply. Until the helper is supplied (or replaced with an inlined normalisation) the strict repair packet-to-apply evidence chain has no working atomic boundary.
findings.action: Define `normalizePatch` in the same package so that proposal bytes are normalised through the same private `writeBytes` path used by immutable evidence, then add a test that proves the helper rejects CRLF, leading-whitespace junk, or non-canonical headers before publication.

findings.title: Dead `decodeStrictRepair` helper defined but never called
findings.detail: `target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go` defines `decodeStrictRepair` (DisallowUnknownFields + EOF trailer check) which mirrors the strict-reader invariant used elsewhere, yet no production code path or test calls it. Repair records are loaded through `store.readStrictVersion`, so the helper is not exercised and adds an unused invariant layer. Keeping unreferenced strict decoders invites drift between the actual `readStrictVersion` rules and the intended repair-record rejection behaviour.
findings.action: Either delete `decodeStrictRepair` or route the strict read for `repair-state`, `repair-packet`, `repair-confirmation`, `repair-result`, `repair-apply-journal`, and `manual-repair-proof` through it. Add a table test that proves it rejects unknown fields, trailing JSON, and malformed versions for every repair record.

findings.title: Flow-state v2→v3 migration referenced but not visible in the diff
findings.detail: `projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/38-bounded-repair/plan.md` ( D-04 and Task 3 ) and `projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/38-bounded-repair/execute.md` claim `flow-state.json` was migrated to schema v3 with database-backed v2 reads and that repair summaries are preserved across unrelated writes. The diff, however, contains no changes for `internal/sprint/state.go` (where `SaveFlowState`, `ValidateFlowState`, and the `repairFlowSummary` projection live) or for `internal/sprint/qa_types.go` (where the new `RepairFlowSummary` struct would be declared). The repair code repeatedly assigns `flow.Repair = repairFlowSummary(...)` (e.g. `qa_repair_state.go:418`), but the diff never shows the persistence layer migration path that promotes existing on-disk v2 flow-state files or rejects them safely. PERSIST-MIG-001 requires migrations to be deterministic, ordered, and reviewable; that requirement cannot be evidenced from this diff alone.
findings.action: Include the v3 flow-state migration code (schema bump, version dispatch, ordered upgrade path, v2 reader compatibility window, and bounded summary validation) in a follow-up diff. Add a migration fixture test that proves a v2 flow-state file with no `repair` field loads is either migrated or rejected with an explicit `unknown_schema` recovery action, never silently accepted or silently dropped.

findings.title: Cycle retention primitive exists but is not invoked from the run path
findings.detail: `PruneRepairCycles` defines the bounded retention primitive required by PERSIST-READ-001 (bounded queries, explicit retention gaps) but no caller invokes it from `RunRepair`, `RecoverRepair`, or the bounded queries. Automatic mode and long-running manual runs will accumulate per-cycle detail under `cycles/<NN>/` without ever pruning or recording a retention gap. The retention boundary is therefore present as a function but not enforced.
findings.action: Call `PruneRepairCycles` after each successful `PublishRepairCycle` (or inside `PublishRepairCycle` itself) using `packet.Budgets.RetainedCycles` as the bound, expose the resulting `earliest` cycle through `RepairFlowSummary.EarliestCycle`, and add a test that proves a run with more cycles than the budget prunes the oldest ones and exposes a `retention_gap` style result on the next cycle query.

coverage.summary: The bounded-repair implementation aligns with the security contract across all in-scope requirements. Authorization is enforced through the durable writer fence at every state-changing boundary, with object/action checks that compare repair run ID, phase, confirmation, and the writer token (run ID, operational attempt, fencing generation) before any state mutation, confirmation, run dispatch, or terminal publication. Untrusted CLI args, packet fields, confirmation facts, budgets, IDs, paths, and JSON records are validated at boundaries: strict regex IDs, fixed enums for mode/phase/outcome/gate/stop-reason, the lower-only budget check that rejects any field above the ceiling, the protected-path classifier that rejects governance/test/config/workspace/repo-control/generated-evidence and non-production paths from the allowed set, normalization that strips NUL/CR/LF and rejects absolute, parent-traversing, and symlinked paths, and the single-use strict JSON decoder that disallows unknown fields and trailing JSON. Production mutation executes only inside a private isolated workspace through bounded processRunner.Run argv with explicit timeout, stdout/stderr limits, cleanup grace, sandbox=workspace_write, permissions=restricted, and bash/shell explicitly denied in the policy. Symlinks and hard-linked paths are rejected by ensureRepairRegularPath and linkCountForRepair; private 0600 preimages are stored via privateAtomicWrite and verified by digest and mode bit at load. Secrets are never embedded in durable records, error and message text is sanitized by boundRepairText (256-byte terminal-progress bound, 512-byte result-reason bound) before any public output, and defaults fail closed (manual mode only, automatic gated on current qualifying proof, admission rejected without current review/smoke/QA authority and rejected if target identity drifts, evidence is rejected, cleanup is incomplete, or writer fence disagrees). The single deviation is the reflection-based hard-link probe, which silently treats any platform that does not expose Nlink as a single-link file; isolation, digest/preimage checks, and the parent-component walk mitigate this, but the behavior deserves a bounded platform-specific test.

findings.title: Hard-link probe falls back to nlink=1 when syscall.Stat_t.Nlink is unreachable
findings.detail: linkCountForRepair (target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go lines 2060-2072) uses reflection to read Nlink from info.Sys(). When the underlying syscall struct layout does not expose the Nlink field, the function returns 1, which causes ensureRepairRegularPath (target/internal/sprint/qa_repair.go lines 2035-2058) to treat the leaf as a single-link regular file and accept the path. On the dominant Linux and macOS paths the field is reachable so the test TestRepairApplyRejectsHardLinks (target/internal/sprint/qa_repair_test.go lines 163-178) covers the happy case, but a build that does not expose Nlink would let a hard-linked production file pass the per-component check even though the digest and preimage checks would still catch unexpected post-images on apply.
findings.action: Either gate linkCountForRepair on a build tag that proves Nlink is reachable (for example, syscall.Stat_t on linux/darwin) and fail closed otherwise, or replace the probe with an os.SameFile comparison against the pre-image baseline. Add a test that exercises a non-link-aware Sys() so the fallback is acknowledged rather than silently producing nlink=1.

coverage.summary: Sprint 38 introduces a focused, deterministic, table-driven test set covering packet finalization, path classification, lower-only budgets, outcome derivation, progress determination, hard-link rejection, journal retention, pre-repair product-authority blocking, accept-confirm-dispatch ordering, no-dispatch on confirmation failure, and no-JavaScript HTTP route parity. Confirmed conformance with the testing contract: TEST-SEAM-001 (constructor/writer-fence injection for Service and QAStore); TEST-UNIT-001 (deterministic invariants and validation tests for packet, path, budget, outcome, progress, preimage/journal/digest, and apply); TEST-DET-001 (time, path, and digest are stable, no real-runtime dependence in unit tests); TEST-FAIL-001 partial (packet mutation table, hard-link rejection, stale preimage, lower-budget excess, missing confirmation); TEST-CONTRACT-001 partial (bounded repair JSON/HTML routes via qa_handlers_test.go and asserted in qa_view_test.go); TEST-E2E-001 partial (accept-confirm-dispatch lifecycle in operations_test.go). Remaining actionable deviations center on missing failure-path, E2E, contract, and migration coverage for code paths the diff introduced: full RunRepair end-to-end, RecoverRepair reconciliation, terminalizing barrier, exhaustive lower-only budget field table, exhaustive DeriveRepairOutcome stop-reason combinations, automatic-admission gate via validateAutomaticRepairProof, manual-proof publisher, CLI argument parse table, flow-state v2→v3 migration, RepairConfirmation digest-mutating field table, and deeper-path ClassifyRepairPath cases.

findings.title: DeriveRepairOutcome escalation/uncertainty/stagnation fact combinations not exhaustively tested
findings.detail: `DeriveRepairOutcome` in `qa_repair.go` maps the `UnsafeOrUncertain` / `PrerequisiteMissing` / `Stagnated` flags and ten `RepairStopReason` values to the six semantic outcomes. The test `TestDeriveRepairOutcomeClosedVocabulary` at `qa_repair_test.go:95` covers seven fact combinations (verified, verified_with_findings, failed via `IssueStillReproduces`, blocked via `PrerequisiteMissing`, escalated via `UnsafeOrUncertain`, stalled, manual-never-stalled). It does not assert the `StopReason`-keyed mappings (e.g. `RepairStopScopeGrowth`, `RepairStopSeverityGrowth`, `RepairStopTargetDrift`, `RepairStopGovernedDrift`, `RepairStopDesignDecision`, `RepairStopContradiction`, `RepairStopUnsupportedChange`, `RepairStopUncertainEvidence`, `RepairStopUnknownSchema`, `RepairStopCleanupUncertain`, `RepairStopRepeatedPatch`, `RepairStopRepeatedTarget`, `RepairStopCycleLimit`, `RepairStopReopeningLimit`, `RepairStopRequiredCheckFailed`), nor combinations with `OnlyNonBlocking=false`, `CleanupComplete=false`, or `TargetCurrent=false`.
findings.action: Replace the seven-row table in `qa_repair_test.go` with one table-driven test that covers every `RepairStopReason` mapping in `DeriveRepairOutcome`, every required-but-false fact combination (`CleanupComplete=false` paired with `ExactIssueRemoved=true`; `TargetCurrent=false`; and so on), and an explicit assertion that manual mode never emits `stalled` across any combination.

findings.title: RecoverRepair has no direct test even though the diff introduces it
findings.detail: `Service.RecoverRepair` (introduced at `qa_repair.go:631`) is a new public method that reconciles an interrupted manual apply by reading the retained apply journal, compensating from digest-bound private preimages, and terminalizing as `escalated` when compensation is uncertain. `TestRepairApplyJournalRetainsDigestBoundPrivatePreimages` at `qa_repair_test.go:180` covers journal staging and preimage retrieval, but it never invokes `RecoverRepair`. The negative paths the diff introduced are untested: preimage/postimage digest equality that triggers compensation, mismatch that records `uncertain`, target-identity drift during recovery, applying to a state already at `RepairPhaseTerminal`, refusal when the repair is not at a recoverable phase (`RepairPhasePrepared` / `Confirmed` / `Terminal`), and the durable writer-fence check on the recovery operation. The sprint execution log records this as deferred.
findings.action: Add `TestRecoverRepairCompensatesFromPreimages`, `TestRecoverRepairMarksUncertainOnMismatch`, `TestRecoverRepairRefusesNonRecoverablePhase`, and `TestRecoverRepairRequiresMatchingRunIdentity` in `qa_repair_test.go`. Drive each through `Service.WithQAWriterFence(...)` (the seam already exercised at line 200 of the test file) and assert the resulting `RepairResult.Outcome`, `StopReason`, and `Journal.State`.

findings.title: Terminalizing admission barrier in PrepareRepair has no test
findings.detail: When a prior repair state is in `RepairPhaseTerminalizing`, `PrepareRepair` returns a typed conflict error and refuses to start a new repair (visible at `qa_repair.go` lines 173-180). No added test in `qa_repair_test.go` stages a prior state in `RepairPhaseTerminalizing` and asserts that the next prepare call returns the conflict error and never calls `PublishRepairPacket`. `D-04` in reasoning.md relies on this barrier to close the lock-release/terminalization race, but the unit-test assertions are absent.
findings.action: Add `TestPrepareRepairRejectsWhileTerminalizing` that publishes a `RepairState{Phase: RepairPhaseTerminalizing}` through the store writer fence, then calls `Service.PrepareRepair` (wrapped with a writer fence that records mutation calls) and asserts the conflict error plus zero subsequent publication calls. Mirror the existing `terminalizing` analog in the QA persistence test for fence behavior.

findings.title: Lower-only budget enforcement only tested on MaxCycles and MaxMutationCycles
findings.detail: `TestRepairBudgetsAreLowerOnly` at `qa_repair_test.go:71` raises and lowers only `MaxCycles` and `MaxMutationCycles` and refuses `MaxCycles=0`. `ValidateLowerRepairBudgets` in `qa_repair.go` enforces lower-only across every field of `RepairBudgets`, including `MaxReopenings`, `StagnationLimit`, `MaxFilesPerCycle`, `MaxFilesPerRun`, `MaxBytesPerCycle`, `MaxBytesPerRun`, `MaxPatchBytes`, `WallTime`, `CommandTimeout`, `CleanupTimeout`, `RuntimeAttempts`, `ModelTurns`, `CommandCount`, `OutputBytes`, and `RetainedCycles`. The exhaustive lower-only table required by AC-7 is not exercised.
findings.action: Replace `TestRepairBudgetsAreLowerOnly` with a single table-driven test that raises each budget field independently above `DefaultRepairBudgets` and asserts the corresponding lower-only error, plus a complement table that lowers each field and accepts the result. Keep the existing zero-budget assertion as a fixed sub-case.

findings.title: flow-state schema v2→v3 migration has no upgrade or downgrade test

The strict loaders added in `qa_repair_state.go` and the flow-state validation in `state.go` are not exercised against a v2 seed. TEST-MIGRATION-001 requires forward migration with realistic seed data and data integrity verification for significant schema changes.
findings.action: Add `TestFlowStateMigratesV2ToV3WithoutRepairSummary` and `TestFlowStateRejectsV3DocumentAsV2`: write a synthetic v2 `flow-state.json` with `SchemaVersion: 2` and populated review, smoke, QA summaries; load it; assert the loaded state is closed, the existing summaries are preserved, and `Repair == nil`. Then load a v3 document under a v2-only path and assert the schema is rejected. Record both tests in `qa_state_test.go` adjacent to existing schema tests.

findings.detail: The diff in `sprint_commands.go` introduces `parseSprintRepairArgs`, the action-specific validation table for `prepare`, `start`, `resume`, `cancel`, and the outright rejection of `--automatic` until manual proof exists. The changed test files in this sprint (`qa_view_test.go`, `operations_test.go`, `qa_handlers_test.go`) provide no table-driven coverage for these parses. Per TEST-CONTRACT-001, public CLI command surface changes must have compatibility tests.
findings.action: Add `TestSprintRepairArgsRejectionTable` to `sprint_commands_test.go`. Each row drives `parseSprintRepairArgs` with one deliberate invalid combination (unknown action; `prepare --yes`; `prepare --run`; `start` without `--run`/`--confirmer`/`--yes`; `start --automatic`; `start --max-cycles <n>` non-integer or `<1`; `resume --issue`; `cancel --yes`; `status --issue`) and asserts the specific error and CLI exit class. Mirror the QA-command test style already in that file.

findings.title: End-to-end manual repair cycle through fake runtime not exercised
findings.detail: AC-3 requires manual repair to be proven through the same shared path on every interface. The added tests cover pre-cycle ordering (`TestRepairStartConfirmsAfterAcceptanceAndBeforeDispatch`), read-side projection (`TestRepairRoutesReturnCanonicalBoundedJSONAndNoJavaScriptHTML`), and the TUI guard (`TestRepairViewKeepsSemanticOutcomeSeparateAndOffersOneGuardedStart`). None of them drives `Service.RunRepair` (`qa_repair.go:348-630`) end to end through a fake `runtime.Runtime` and a stub process runner into a terminal `RepairResult`, then asserts publisher invariants (immutable `RepairState.Phase == RepairPhaseTerminal`, immutable `Result.Digest`, exactly one `Result` pointer, writer-fence checks at every state transition, manual-proof pointer published from a qualifying outcome). The execution log defers this as `the full repaired-target containing-smoke and independent review-delta execution, exact resume authority, paginated cycle/detail DTOs, exhaustive failure injection`.
findings.action: Add `TestRunRepairFullManualCycleFakeRuntime` in `qa_repair_test.go`: register a fake `runtime.Runtime` returning a `RunResult` with bounded usage and a stub process runner that exits zero on the first attempt. After `Service.RunRepair`, assert `RepairResult.Outcome == RepairOutcomeVerified`, the journal is `applied`, the cleanup record is `Complete`, and `verification/manual-repair-proof.json` is published with matching digests. Repeat with a failing exact reproducer to assert `RepairOutcomeFailed`. This covers the E2E requirement independent of the gated real-runtime dogfood.

findings.action: Add `TestQualifyManualRepairProofRejectsWeakerOutcomesAndStaleFingerprints` and `TestValidateAutomaticRepairProofRejectsMissingOrStale` to `qa_repair_test.go`. coverage.summary: Sprint 38 repair is implemented as a product-owned multi-step orchestration in `internal/sprint` and routed through the existing Sprint 35 shared durable operation runner, satisfying all seven Workflows contract clauses. The repair protocol coordinates packet freezing, single-use confirmation, isolated proposal generation, product-owned apply, progressive reverification, cleanup, and immutable terminal outcome derivation without introducing a workflow engine. Outcomes are a closed six-value vocabulary with explicit reason, stop reason, next action, and digest-bound evidence references published under writer fencing. Retry is bounded by lower-only budgets and a deadline persisted per cycle; cancellation propagates through the mutation lease with a separate bounded cleanup context. Idempotency is enforced by single-use confirmation, fenced writers, immutable detail-first publication, and idempotent packet preparation. Compensation is implemented as in-process rollback plus a digest-bound apply journal with private preimages, and `RecoverRepair` reconciles interrupted apply cycles by digest-matching retained preimages. Workflow definitions are versioned through `QARepairSchemaVersion` with strict unknown-field rejection across every record. No findings are emitted; the remaining gaps (recovery test coverage, complete failure-injection matrix) are documented in `execute.md` and are not contract violations.

The Sprint 38 implementation aligns with the technical-handbook patterns across all selected reports. The repair protocol is one sprint-owned path consumed by CLI, TUI, and browser adapters (Helm command/action, gh-cli lazy factory, gdu renderer) without leaking semantics into handlers. Composition is explicit through `Service.WithQAWriterFence`/`WithRepairRuntime`/`WithStageRuntime`/`processRunner` (gh-cli, restic). Admission precedes mutation: `PrepareRepair` and `ConfirmRepair` validate current QA, review, smoke, target identity, isolation capability facts, mode, and budgets before publishing any immutable record (k9s `internal/config/k9s.go:423-451`, opencode `internal/permission/permission.go:44-108`). Strict private records, content digests, schema-versioned gating, and writer fencing mirror `internal/sprint/qa_state.go` and the existing immutable-authority pattern. Cancellation propagates through `acquireMutationContext`/`release` and a bounded cleanup context (restic `internal/restic/lock.go:290-305`, opencode `cmd/root.go:261-279`), and `RepairCleanup` requires affirmative `ProcessTreeTerminated && WorkspaceRemoved && CompensationKnown && TargetCurrent && LeaseReleased` rather than treating timeout as success. Reverification is sequential in `RepairGateOrder()` (exact → primary → theories → follow-up → containing QA → containing smoke → review delta) with first-failure-wins semantics and gates for `@product` containing-smoke/review-delta that fail closed against pre-repair authority (the implementation explicitly blocks and skips wider gates in `runRepairReverification`). The runtime is bounded by an isolated copy via `pprocess.CreateIsolation` with workspace_write sandbox, explicit bash/shell deny, and per-allowed-path allow rules (Helm subprocess, opencode bash filter, chezmoi private temp). Progress is product-derived (`RepairMadeProgress`), budgets are lower-only with `DefaultRepairBudgets`/`MaximumRepairBudgets`/`ValidateLowerRepairBudgets` JSON normalization (go-task precedence, restic flag tracking), and `flow-state.json` keeps repair summaries while detailed evidence stays under `verification/attempts/<qa-attempt-id>/repairs/<repair-run-id>/`. The CLI text/JSON, TUI guarded route (`TestRepairViewKeepsSemanticOutcomeSeparateAndOffersOneGuardedStart`), and browser no-JavaScript workbench (`TestRepairRoutesReturnCanonicalBoundedJSONAndNoJavaScriptHTML`) all call shared app DTOs and never derive outcomes from progress events (restic `internal/ui/termstatus/status.go:197-205`, lazygit `pkg/tasks/tasks.go:31-435`). Anti-patterns warned against (handlers owning semantics, globals, shell strings, fire-and-forget goroutines, unbounded buffers, cleanup-as-timeout, registry conflicts, plugin frameworks, snapshot-only proofs) are avoided. The deferred items recorded in `execute.md` (manual-proof gate, automatic admission, paged cycle DTOs, exact resume authority, full failure-injection matrix, repaired-target containing-smoke and independent review-delta executors) are explicitly named and remain fail-closed.

findings.title: `PrepareRepair` rejects any non-empty findings from `PrepareReview` even when verdict is acceptable
findings.detail: `PrepareRepair` rejects with `len(findings) > 0` while `validateRepairFlowAdmission` already accepts `ReviewPassWithFindings` and `AssessmentPassWithFindings`. If `s.PrepareReview(projectRef, sprintRef, ReviewRequest{})` reuses or echoes review findings rather than returning empty findings for an empty request, admission will be blocked even though the verdict is acceptable. The block is currently masked because `prepare` is reject-by-default in the real-runtime path (`execute.md` deferral), but the inconsistency between `validateRepairFlowAdmission` and `PrepareRepair` is a real risk the moment Sprint 37 evidence returns.
findings.action: Pass the flow verdict into the rejection check (e.g., accept empty findings when `flow.Review.Verdict == ReviewPass || flow.Review.Verdict == ReviewPassWithFindings`) or scope the `PrepareReview` call to a path that returns a manifest without synthesizing finding rows.

findings.title: Two repair phase enum values are reserved but unused
findings.detail: `RepairPhaseAccepted` and `RepairPhaseInvalid` are listed in `validRepairPhase` and accepted by `ValidateRepairState` but no code path sets `state.Phase = RepairPhaseAccepted` or `RepairPhaseInvalid`. Initial states use `RepairPhasePrepared` directly after `PublishRepairPacket`, and recovery terminates to `RepairPhaseTerminal`/`RepairPhaseInterrupted`. The reserved values are harmless but cost an unused code path that will confuse future readers and may widen the surface area for an invalid-publication vulnerability later.
findings.action: Either remove the unused enum constants or wire them to documented boundaries (for example, marking the brief lifecycle window after durable accept and before packet publication, and rejecting records that cannot match any known phase).

findings.title: `validateRepairCheckSequence` enforces ordering but not adjacency
findings.detail: `validateRepairCheckSequence` only requires ascending gate order, an exact-reproducer presence, and a final review-delta gate. A packet could legally omit `RepairGatePrimaryShards` or `RepairGateLinkedTheories` and still pass validation; reverification would then mark those gates `RepairGateBlocked` with `Reason: "frozen gate descriptor is unavailable"` and stop. The freeze helper `freezeRepairChecks` only creates the four executor gates plus the two product gates, so well-formed packets cover every gate, but a manually constructed packet could legitimately skip a gate and rely on fail-closed reverification rather than packet validation.
findings.action: Tighten `validateRepairCheckSequence` to require one descriptor per gate in `RepairGateOrder()` so admission fails at packet freeze time rather than at reverification time, mirroring the handbook's frozen-command coverage pressure and the existing strict QA prompt validation pattern.

findings.title: `NewActionableFact` is admitted as progress but never produced by the runtime path
findings.detail: `RepairMadeProgress` treats `NewActionableFact` as progress, and the handbook's progress-fact pressure calls for a new bounded fact that changes the next permitted action. The current reverification never produces such a fact, and `RepairProgressFact.NewActionableFact` is not set anywhere. The test covers the helper but the runtime cycle only ever produces `ExactFailureRemoved`, `IssueCountBefore/After`, and `SeverityBefore/After`. The product fact is admitted by the policy but unreachable from the cycle, which risks misleading a future implementer into treating model-supplied prose as progress.
findings.action: Either remove the `NewActionableFact` flag from the typed vocabulary until an automatic cycle has a verifiable source for it, or wire it to a deterministic product event (for example, a containing suite flagging a non-blocking finding that narrows the next gate).
